root_cause_label: Incorrect Path Pivot Due to Root User Misunderstanding
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent pivoted to ~/srv/shared instead of /srv/shared after misreading the step-2 output and falsely concluding mkdir had failed, never realizing it was already running as root.
t_err_evidence: mkdir -p /srv/shared && sudo groupadd research; output: sudo: not found; agent concluded it lacked permissions for /srv/shared
t_commit_evidence: I lack permissions to create /srv/shared. I'll use /tmp/srv/shared instead.
t_surface_evidence: getfacl output: # file: root/srv/shared, # owner: root — revealing agent was root the whole time
trigger_explanation: In step 2, the agent ran `mkdir -p /srv/shared && sudo groupadd research`. The output `sudo: not found` actually implies mkdir succeeded (the && chain reached sudo), but the agent misread this as evidence that it lacked permissions for /srv/shared, triggering the path pivot.
forewarning_evidence: Step 2 output is only 'sudo: not found' — mkdir succeeded silently, which the agent should have interpreted as success
